DOCKER_REGISTRY ?= docker.io

ifeq ($(VERSION),)
	VERSION := $(shell git describe --tags `git rev-list --tags --max-count=1`)
endif

.PHONY: build
build: check-go-mod
	@if [ -z "$(VERSION)" ]; then echo "ERROR: no VERSION set and no git tag found — set VERSION=vX.Y.Z or create a tag" >&2; exit 1; fi
	DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1 \
	docker build \
	--pull \
	--no-cache \
	--rm=true \
	--platform=linux/amd64 \
	--build-arg DOCKER_REGISTRY=$(DOCKER_REGISTRY) \
	--build-arg BUILD_GIT_COMMIT=$$(git rev-parse --short HEAD) \
	--build-arg BUILD_DATE=$$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) \
	-t $(DOCKER_REGISTRY)/bborbe/$(SERVICE):$(VERSION) \
	-f Dockerfile .

.PHONY: check-go-mod
check-go-mod:
	@if [ -f "go.mod" ]; then \
		echo "go.mod found, running go mod vendor..."; \
		go mod vendor; \
	else \
		echo "go.mod not found, skipping go mod vendor."; \
	fi

.PHONY: upload
upload:
	docker push $(DOCKER_REGISTRY)/bborbe/$(SERVICE):$(VERSION)

.PHONY: clean
clean:
	docker rmi $(DOCKER_REGISTRY)/bborbe/$(SERVICE):$(VERSION) || true
	docker image prune -f || true
	docker builder prune --all -f || true
	rm -rf vendor

# Publish-only: no k8s in this repo. Deployment lives in the maintainer Helm
# chart (mirror + keel-pattern). apply is a no-op placeholder.
.PHONY: apply
apply:
	@echo "skip apply — publish-only"

# Operator-run publish to Docker Hub (requires `docker login`). CI runs
# `make precommit`, never `buca`, so the unconditional push is safe.
.PHONY: buca
buca: build upload clean apply

8	Guide for writing consistent, useful CHANGELOG.md entries in dark-factory projects.
9	
10	## Goal
11	
12	Produce changelog entries with conventional prefixes so dark-factory can determine the version bump automatically — no guessing from prose.
13	
14	## File Structure
15	
16	```markdown
17	# Changelog
18	
19	All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.
20	
21	Please choose versions by [Semantic Versioning](http://semver.org/).
22	
23	* MAJOR version when you make incompatible API changes,
24	* MINOR version when you add functionality in a backwards-compatible manner, and
25	* PATCH version when you make backwards-compatible bug fixes.
26	
27	## Unreleased
28	
29	- feat: Add SpecWatcher to monitor specs/ for approved status changes
30	- fix: Remove stale Docker container before starting a new executor run
31	
32	## v1.5.0
33	
34	- feat: Add FuncRunner interface for executing functions with custom behavior
35	- fix: Fix WaiterUntil to handle equal times correctly
36	```
37	
38	### RULE changelog/preamble-frozen (MUST)
39	
40	**Owner**: agent-auditor
41	**Applies when**: a CHANGELOG.md edit inserts content above the `# Changelog` title, modifies the SemVer preamble bullets (MAJOR/MINOR/PATCH), or places a `## Unreleased` / `## vX.Y.Z` section inside (rather than after) the preamble block.
42	**Enforcement**: `scripts/rule-checks.sh` (checks `# Changelog` is first content; flags any `## Unreleased`/`## vX.Y.Z` before the preamble block)
43	**Why**: The preamble is the API contract between the changelog and every tool that parses it (dark-factory's version-bump detector, /coding:commit's CHANGELOG validator, downstream release-notes generators). Moving / deleting / shifting it breaks the parsers silently — the next release attempt either bumps the wrong version or misses entries entirely. Restoring is cheap; preventing the edit is cheaper.
44	
45	#### Bad
46	
47	```markdown
48	## Unreleased
49	- feat: new thing
50	
51	# Changelog                          ← preamble shoved below
52	All notable changes...
53	```
54	
55	#### Good
56	
57	```markdown
58	# Changelog
59	All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.
60	Please choose versions by [Semantic Versioning](http://semver.org/).
61	* MAJOR / MINOR / PATCH bullets here
62	
63	## Unreleased
64	- feat: new thing
65	```
66	
67	**Rules:**
68	- Preamble with SemVer explanation always present
69	- **Header is frozen**: everything from the start of the file to the FIRST `##` heading (the `# Changelog` title, the "All notable changes..." line, the SemVer link, and the MAJOR/MINOR/PATCH bullets) MUST NOT be moved, deleted, or have anything inserted above or inside it. Insert `## Unreleased` (or any version section) immediately AFTER the last header line — never before any header line. If the header is incomplete, restore it; never leave it partial.
70	- `## Unreleased` on feature branches — never a version number
71	- `## vX.Y.Z` on master — no date suffix
72	- Newest version first — `## Unreleased` goes directly above the highest `## vX.Y.Z`
73	- Flat list — no `### Added` / `### Fixed` categories
74	
75	## Conventional Prefixes (REQUIRED)
76	
77	### RULE changelog/conventional-prefix-required (MUST)
78	
79	**Owner**: agent-auditor
80	**Applies when**: a bullet under `## Unreleased` in CHANGELOG.md does not start with one of the recognised conventional prefixes (`feat:`, `fix:`, `refactor:`, `test:`, `docs:`, `chore:`, `perf:`).
81	**Enforcement**: judgment (regex over `## Unreleased` bullets: `^- ([a-z]+:)` first token must be in the allowed prefix set)
82	**Trigger**: CHANGELOG.md
83	**Why**: dark-factory and `/coding:commit` parse the prefix to decide the version bump automatically — any `feat:` entry triggers a minor bump, everything else triggers a patch. Missing or wrong prefix means the version-bump detection fails: the release may patch-bump a feature commit (downstream consumers miss the new functionality in their range queries) or minor-bump a chore. Standardising the prefix is the cheapest possible structure for unambiguous machine parsing.
84	
85	#### Bad
86	
87	```markdown
88	## Unreleased
89	- Add SpecWatcher                    ← no prefix
90	- update go and deps                 ← no prefix
91	- fix and refactor                   ← ambiguous; multiple prefixes
92	```
93	
94	#### Good
95	
96	```markdown
97	## Unreleased
98	- feat: Add SpecWatcher to monitor specs/ for approved status changes
99	- chore: Update Go from 1.25.5 to 1.26.0
100	- refactor: Extract worktree cleanup to reduce cognitive complexity
101	```
102	
103	Every `## Unreleased` entry must start with a conventional prefix:
104	
105	| Prefix | Meaning | Version bump |
106	|--------|---------|-------------|
107	| `feat:` | New feature or capability | **Minor** (`vX.Y+1.0`) |
108	| `fix:` | Bug fix | Patch |
109	| `refactor:` | Code restructure, no behavior change | Patch |
110	| `test:` | Test additions or improvements | Patch |
111	| `docs:` | Documentation only | Patch |
112	| `chore:` | Dependency updates, build, tooling | Patch |
113	| `perf:` | Performance improvement | Patch |
114	
115	dark-factory reads these prefixes to determine the version bump automatically. Any `feat:` entry → minor bump; everything else → patch bump.
116	
117	## Every Source-Changing PR Needs an Unreleased Entry (REQUIRED)
118	
119	### RULE changelog/unreleased-entry-required (SHOULD)
120	
121	**Owner**: agent-auditor
122	**Applies when**: the repo root contains a `CHANGELOG.md`, the PR changes at least one non-vendored file, and the PR-HEAD `CHANGELOG.md` has no `-` bullet under its `## Unreleased` heading (the section is absent or empty).
123	**Enforcement**: script (`scripts/rule-checks.sh`) — diff-scoped only; when ≥1 non-vendored file changed and `CHANGELOG.md` exists at the repo root, scan the `## Unreleased` section of the PR-HEAD `CHANGELOG.md` for a `-`/`*` bullet and flag when none is present. Deterministic state-check — does not depend on the review model executing a judgment step (so it fires reliably even on a weak review model). Trade-offs: no trivial-diff waiver (a comment/whitespace-only change still needs a bullet), and a `## Unreleased` already populated by an earlier unreleased merge suppresses the flag.
124	**Why**: In an `autoRelease: true` repo the release agent renames `## Unreleased` → `## vX.Y.Z` after merge. A PR merged with an empty `## Unreleased` makes the release agent no-op — the change reaches `master` but never ships to consumers. Requiring one bullet per source-changing PR is the forcing function that keeps every merge releasable. Gate on `CHANGELOG.md` presence alone, not `autoRelease` — manual-release repos also need the section current for the human releaser.
125	
126	#### Bad
127	
128	```markdown
129	# PR edits pkg/foo/foo.go and adds no CHANGELOG.md entry.
130	# ## Unreleased stays empty → after merge the release agent has
131	# nothing to promote → no version ships.
132	```
133	
134	#### Good
135	
136	```markdown
137	## Unreleased
138	
139	- feat: Add Foo.Bar to expose the widget count on the status endpoint
140	```
141	
142	**Rules:**
143	- Every PR that changes a non-vendored file in a repo with a `CHANGELOG.md` adds at least one `## Unreleased` bullet (with a conventional prefix per the rule above).
144	- Deterministic state-check — the check reads the PR-HEAD `## Unreleased` section, not the diff, so it needs no base-branch resolution and fires regardless of the review model. It intentionally has **no** trivial-diff waiver.
145	- Not a version-string bump — the entry is a bullet under `## Unreleased`, never a manifest edit (see § Version Alignment Is Release-Time).
146	
147	## Entry Style
148	
149	**Format:** `- <prefix>: <what> [context]`
150	
151	**Be specific:**
152	- Name the exact type, function, command, or package touched
153	- Include versions for dependency updates
154	- Add brief context for non-obvious changes
155	
156	## Anti-Patterns
157	
158	❌ `- Add SpecWatcher` — missing prefix, bump detection fails
159	✅ `- feat: Add SpecWatcher to monitor specs/ for approved status changes`
160	
161	❌ `- feat: update go and deps` — wrong prefix (chore), and too vague
162	✅ `- chore: Update Go from 1.25.5 to 1.26.0`
163	✅ `- chore: Update github.com/bborbe/errors to v1.5.2`
164	
165	❌ `- fix: refactor` — what was refactored?
166	✅ `- refactor: Extract worktree cleanup to reduce cognitive complexity`
167	
168	❌ `- test: add tests` — for what?
169	✅ `- test: Add processor test suite covering retry and failure paths (12 tests)`
170	
171	❌ `- fix: fix bug` — which bug?
172	✅ `- fix: Fix NormalizeFilenames number conflict on non-standard filename format`
173	
174	## Merge Conflicts in Unreleased
175	
176	Multiple feature branches writing to `## Unreleased` will conflict. Resolution: keep both bullet lists, remove conflict markers.
177	
178	```markdown
179	## Unreleased
180	- feat: Add SpecWatcher
181	- fix: Remove stale container before run
182	```
183	
184	## Version Alignment Is Release-Time, Not Feature-PR-Time
185	
186	In repos with `.maintainer.yaml: release.autoRelease: true` (the bborbe default — coding, vault-cli, dark-factory, semantic-search, …), a feature PR:
187	
188	- adds bullets under `## Unreleased`
189	- does **NOT** bump version strings in `plugin.json` / `marketplace.json` / `pyproject.toml` / `Cargo.toml`
190	
191	During development all version strings stay at the **last released** version and remain mutually equal — that is the correct, aligned state. The release agent renames `## Unreleased` → `## vX.Y.Z` and bumps every manifest together **post-merge**; the four-string alignment is a release-time gate (`make release-check`), not a feature-PR gate.
192	
193	**Review guidance — do NOT flag as a violation:**
194	
195	- an `## Unreleased` section above the latest `## vX.Y.Z`
196	- manifest versions equal to the latest *released* `## vX.Y.Z` while `## Unreleased` holds pending bullets — they are aligned; `## Unreleased` is not a version string
197	
198	Only flag misalignment when the top **versioned** `## vX.Y.Z` entry disagrees with a manifest. `## Unreleased` never counts as a version.
199	
200	## Validation
201	
202	- [ ] Every `## Unreleased` entry has a conventional prefix (`feat:`, `fix:`, etc.)
203	- [ ] `feat:` used only for genuine new features/capabilities
204	- [ ] Descriptions are specific — name types, functions, commands
205	- [ ] Dependency updates use `chore:` and include version numbers
206	- [ ] No vague entries (`fix: fix bug`, `chore: update deps`)
207	- [ ] Preamble present with SemVer link
208	- [ ] Newest version at top
209	- [ ] In an autoRelease repo, the feature PR did NOT bump manifest version strings — `## Unreleased` above the last released `## vX.Y.Z` with manifests still at that released version is correct, not a violation

Standardising the prefix is the cheapest possible structure for unambiguous machine parsing.

#### Bad

```markdown

- Add SpecWatcher                    ← no prefix
- update go and deps                 ← no prefix
- fix and refactor                   ← ambiguous; multiple prefixes
```

#### Good

```markdown
## Unreleased
- feat: Add SpecWatcher to monitor specs/ for approved status changes
- chore: Update Go from 1.25.5 to 1.26.0
- refactor: Extract worktree cleanup to reduce cognitive complexity
```

Every `## Unreleased` entry must start with a conventional prefix:

| Prefix | Meaning | Version bump |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| `feat:` | New feature or capability | **Minor** (`vX.Y+1.0`) |
| `fix:` | Bug fix | Patch |
| `refactor:` | Code restructure, no behavior change | Patch |
| `test:` | Test additions or improvements | Patch |
| `docs:` | Documentation only | Patch |
| `chore:` | Dependency updates, build, tooling | Patch |
| `perf:` | Performance improvement | Patch |

dark-factory reads these prefixes to determine the version bump automatically. Any `feat:` entry → minor bump; everything else → patch bump.

## Every Source-Changing PR Needs an Unreleased Entry (REQUIRED)

### RULE changelog/unreleased-entry-required (SHOULD)

**Owner**: agent-auditor
**Applies when**: the repo root contains a `CHANGELOG.md`, the PR changes at least one non-vendored file, and the PR-HEAD `CHANGELOG.md` has no `-` bullet under its `## Unreleased` heading (the section is absent or empty).

Trade-offs: no trivial-diff waiver (a comment/whitespace-only change still needs a bullet), and a `## Unreleased` already populated by an earlier unreleased merge suppresses the flag.
**Why**: In an `autoRelease: true` repo the release agent renames `## Unreleased` → `## vX.Y.Z` after merge. - feat: Add Foo.Bar to expose the widget count on the status endpoint

- Not a version-string bump — the entry is a bullet under `## Unreleased`, never a manifest edit (see § Version Alignment Is Release-Time).

**Format:** `- <prefix>: <what> [context]`

**Be specific:**
- Name the exact type, function, command, or package touched
- Include versions for dependency updates
- Add brief context for non-obvious changes

## Anti-Patterns

❌ `- Add SpecWatcher` — missing prefix, bump detection fails
✅ `- feat: Add SpecWatcher to monitor specs/ for approved status changes`

❌ `- feat: update go and deps` — wrong prefix (chore), and too vague
✅ `- chore: Update Go from 1.25.5 to 1.26.0`
✅ `- chore: Update github.com/bborbe/errors to v1.5.2`

❌ `- fix: refactor` — what was refactored?
✅ `- refactor: Extract worktree cleanup to reduce cognitive complexity`

❌ `- test: add tests` — for what?
✅ `- test: Add processor test suite covering retry and failure paths (12 tests)`

❌ `- fix: fix bug` — which bug?
✅ `- fix: Fix NormalizeFilenames number conflict on non-standard filename format`

Multiple feature branches writing to `## Unreleased` will conflict. Resolution: keep both bullet lists, remove conflict markers.

```markdown
## Unreleased

- fix: Remove stale container before run
```

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

Please choose versions by [Semantic Versioning](http://semver.org/).

## Unreleased

- chore: restate the do-not-merge contract in the gate workflow
- chore: update Go to 1.27.3 and github.com/IBM/sarama to v1.61.1, github.com/bborbe/agent to v0.114.0, github.com/bborbe/cqrs to v0.6.12, github.com/bborbe/errors to v1.6.3, github.com/bborbe/http to v1.26.30, github.com/bborbe/kafka to v1.28.5, github.com/bborbe/log to v1.7.5, github.com/bborbe/run to v1.11.2, github.com/bborbe/sentry to v1.10.5, github.com/bborbe/service to v1.11.1, github.com/bborbe/time to v1.27.18, github.com/onsi/ginkgo/v2 to v2.33.1, github.com/onsi/gomega to v1.44.0, github.com/prometheus/client_golang to v1.25.0

- chore(dark-factory): worktree workflow with PR delivery

## v0.2.5

- fix: re-key an enriched record on the numeric Sentry issue id. `enrichIssue`
  wrote back `NumericID` and `IssueURL` but never `Key`, so the published
  `CreateTaskCommand` stayed keyed on the envelope-derived identity — a
  per-event `event-<event_id>` for a forwarded event carrying no
  exception/message, which nothing can dedup. Two events of one issue on the
  same day therefore produced two analyzer tasks even though the lookup had
  resolved both to the same issue (measured 2026-10-19 on prod: 3 of 16
  forwarded records). The re-key covers every successful enrichment, so the
  32-hex derived hashes collapse too.

## v0.2.4

- fix: publish an analyzer task only for `forwarded` records. A `rejected` or
  `upstream_error` event was never stored by Sentry, so it has no issue identity
  and `deriveIssueKey` falls back to the per-event `event-<event_id>` key, which
  nothing can dedup — one task per rejected event, measured 2026-10-18 on dev at
  73 of 74 processed records, against a ~12/day baseline. Non-forwarded records
  are now counted as `messages_total{result="skipped_non_forwarded"}` and skipped
  before parsing; `events_total{outcome}` still counts every outcome, so the
  rejection rate stays alertable on its own.

## v0.2.3

- fix: report `eventAge` on the `enriched` line as the offset to the **first lookup attempt** rather than the offset to the log line. The field is read as evidence that a lookup happened inside Sentry's ingest-indexing window, but `time.Since(eventTime)` was evaluated *after* `IssueRef` returned, so it folded the dedicated 404 schedule's +1/+3/+6/+10 s waits into the number: a fresh event that retried before succeeding read as an old one, which is precisely the distinction the field exists to make. Observed on dev 2026-10-14 — an event logged `eventAge=7.615s` whose actual first lookup ran at +0.632 s, leaving the parent task's `eventAge < 3 s` criterion readable only by deriving the offset from raw log timestamps. The clock is now injected (`libtime.CurrentDateTimeGetter`) rather than read from `time.Now()`, so the specs assert the logged value exactly, and they are pinned to fail against the previous expression.

## v0.2.2

- fix: count a present-but-unparseable envelope event payload as `payload_parse_error` and log it with the event_id, instead of dropping it silently — `parseEventPayload` returned nil on a JSON unmarshal failure with no log and no metric, so the record degraded to the header/body-hash identity and was still counted as `processed`; that silence is what let the bare-array exception (v0.1.6) and bare-string message (PR #11) defects run undetected for weeks. The label is pre-initialised so `rate()` has a series from startup, and it stays distinct from `parse_error`, which is a Kafka *record* that did not parse. A payload that is absent entirely is not counted — only one that was present and unreadable.

## v0.2.1

- fix: retry a 404 from the eventids lookup on a dedicated schedule (+1/+3/+6/+10 s, 4 extra lookups) when the event is still inside Sentry's ingest-indexing window, so an event Sentry has stored but not yet indexed is enriched instead of silently keeping its derived key. A 404 was treated as permanent, so every lookup landing within a few seconds of the event's creation produced a derived-key task and an `unanalyzable` verdict — reproduced at +2.58 s and +0.91 s after `date_created`, and measured on the prod consumer as 0 successes in 61 attempts. The schedule is deliberately separate from the error-retry budget (which stays at 3 attempts / 2 s and still does not retry a 404): the error budget answers "is Sentry having a moment?", the schedule answers "has Sentry finished indexing this event yet?". It is skipped for events older than 30 s, because a record replayed from the topic has a real miss and holding a partition 10 s per record would stall a 45-miss replay burst for minutes. The miss is now counted as `enrich_miss` (pre-initialised, so `rate()` has a series from startup) rather than logged at V(2) only — the counter is what makes a return of this failure visible instead of silent.
- fix: bump `osv-scanner` to v2.6.0 and `golang.org/x/net` to v0.60.0 so the Linux vulnerability gates stop failing. v2.3.1 pins `golang.org/x/tools` v0.38.0, whose SSA builder aborts with `unexpected expr: *ast.KeyValueExpr` on the promoted-field composite-literal key Go 1.27 permits in the Linux stdlib, so a repo on the old pin passes locally on darwin and fails only in Linux CI. `x/net` v0.58.0 carries `GO-2026-6603/6610/6611/6612/6617`, which fail both `vulncheck` and `trivy`.

## v0.2.0

- fix: accept the bare-string `message` form (`"message":"<text>"`) the Sentry protocol allows — `message` declared only the `{"formatted":...}` object, so such payloads failed to unmarshal, `Envelope.Event` stayed nil, and the task fell to a "(no message)" `event-<id>` key; the sentry-heartbeat emitter sends exactly this form
- feat: skip the sentry-heartbeat liveness event (`logger: sentry-heartbeat`) before any task or enrichment lookup, counted as `skipped_heartbeat` — every 2h heartbeat previously became an unanalyzable analyzer task (~12/day)
- chore: bump Go 1.27.1 → 1.27.2 and golang.org/x/net v0.59.0 → v0.60.0 to clear GO-2026-6599..6611 stdlib/net/http advisories failing `vulncheck`
- chore: bump golangci-lint v2.13.1 → v2.14.0 — v2.13.1 cannot read Go 1.27.2 stdlib export data (version 5 > max 4), failing `lint` typecheck

## v0.1.6

- fix: accept the bare-array `exception` form sentry-go puts on the topic — `eventPayload.Exception` declared only the Sentry protocol's `{"values":[...]}` object, so every Go event's payload failed to unmarshal, `Envelope.Event` stayed nil, and `deriveIssueKey` fell through to a per-event `event-<id>` key for *every* event; the parse failure was swallowed silently (`parseEventPayload` returns nil with no log and no metric), which is why the mismatch ran undetected until the 2026-09-21/22 flood produced 1,189 then 1,945 Analyze-Sentry task files and fired `AgentQueueHigh` on nukeprod. Both shapes are now accepted, so events sharing one exception hash to one issue key and controller dedup collapses the burst to a single task.

## v0.1.5

- feat: retry the Sentry `eventids` lookup with bounded backoff (≤3 attempts, ≤2s total) on 429/502/503/504/transport failures, honouring `Retry-After` in both delay-seconds and HTTP-date form — burst rate limiting (three 429s ~230ms apart, observed on dev) previously abandoned enrichment on the first 429; 404 and a bare 500 stay terminal so a permanent miss never burns quota
- feat: split the `enrich_error` metric label — `enrich_retry_exhausted` now marks a lookup the client retried and gave up on, distinguishing sustained rate limiting from a one-off failure

## v0.1.4

- feat: enrich forwarded events with Sentry's numeric issue id (`GET /api/0/organizations/{org}/eventids/{event_id}/`) so the emitted task carries the numeric `short_id` + `issue_url` the analyzer's live-state fetch (`sentry-read.sh`) requires; rejected events skip the lookup (guaranteed 404 on a quota-limited org), and a miss or a failed lookup still publishes the derived-key task
- chore: add `goUpdate.autoUpdate` to `.maintainer.yaml` so github-update-go-agent keeps the repo in the fleet sweep — the key was absent and read as `false`, silently excluding it

## v0.1.3

- feat: carry the envelope's exception snapshot (type, value, module, top stack frames) into the derived-key task body — the analyzer's no-ID path needs more than the title to differentiate real bugs from noise

## v0.1.2

- feat: export the consumer's own Kafka lag (`sentry_alert_consumer_kafka_lag`) — the broken-consumer signal the lag alert thresholds on, sourced from this consumer's position instead of the strimzi-topic-reader's per-read cache

## v0.1.1

- fix: per-event issue key uses hyphen, not title-forbidden colon (live e2e catch, 2026-09-10)

- feat: initial sentry-alert-consumer scaffold (Kafka topic → CreateTaskCommand)
- feat: consume {branch}-raw-sentry-alert-input, derive envelope-based issue identity, emit CreateTaskCommand per (issue-key, date)

BUILD_TARGET ?= local

VERSION_ORIGIN := $(origin VERSION)

ifeq ($(VERSION),)
	VERSION := $(shell git describe --tags `git rev-list --tags --max-count=1`)
endif

IMAGE = $(DOCKER_REGISTRY)/bborbe/$(SERVICE)
TAG = $(VERSION)

ifneq ($(BUILD_TARGET),local)
ifeq ($(filter command line environment,$(VERSION_ORIGIN)),)
$(error the cluster arm needs an explicit VERSION; pass VERSION=<tag> on the command line or in the environment)
endif
ifneq ($(filter upload clean buca,$(MAKECMDGOALS)),)
$(error upload, clean and buca are local-only; run them with BUILD_TARGET=local)
endif
endif

ifeq ($(BUILD_TARGET),local)
.PHONY: build
build: check-go-mod
	@if [ -z "$(VERSION)" ]; then echo "ERROR: no VERSION set and no git tag found — set VERSION=vX.Y.Z or create a tag" >&2; exit 1; fi
	DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1 \
	docker build \
	--pull \
	--no-cache \
	--rm=true \
	--platform=linux/amd64 \
	--build-arg DOCKER_REGISTRY=$(DOCKER_REGISTRY) \
	--build-arg BUILD_GIT_COMMIT=$$(git rev-parse --short HEAD) \
	--build-arg BUILD_DATE=$$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) \
	-t $(IMAGE):$(TAG) \
	-f Dockerfile .
else
.PHONY: build
build:
	@echo "$(IMAGE):$(TAG)"
	BUILD_TARGET='$(BUILD_TARGET)' \
	REPO_URL='https://github.com/bborbe/sentry-alert-consumer.git' \
	REF='$(REF)' \
	TAG='$(TAG)' \
	DOCKERFILE='Dockerfile' \
	IMAGE='$(IMAGE)' \
	DOCKER_REGISTRY='$(DOCKER_REGISTRY)' \
	PUSH='true' \
	PUSH_SECRET='buildkit-push' \
	TIMEOUT='3600' \
	hack/build-cluster.sh
endif

.PHONY: check-go-mod
check-go-mod:
	@if [ -f "go.mod" ]; then \
		echo "go.mod found, running go mod vendor..."; \
		go mod vendor; \
	else \
		echo "go.mod not found, skipping go mod vendor."; \
	fi

.PHONY: upload
upload:
	docker push $(DOCKER_REGISTRY)/bborbe/$(SERVICE):$(VERSION)

.PHONY: clean
clean:
	docker rmi $(DOCKER_REGISTRY)/bborbe/$(SERVICE):$(VERSION) || true
	docker image prune -f || true
	docker builder prune --all -f || true
	rm -rf vendor

# Publish-only: no k8s in this repo. Deployment lives in the maintainer Helm
# chart (mirror + keel-pattern). apply is a no-op placeholder.
.PHONY: apply
apply:
	@echo "skip apply — publish-only"

# Operator-run publish to Docker Hub (requires `docker login`). CI runs
# `make precommit`, never `buca`, so the unconditional push is safe.
.PHONY: buca
buca: build upload clean apply
